questions.prompt: HR creates an employee record. What still needs verification before calling the employee app-ready?

options.text: Identity propagation, intended assignments, target accounts and required access
options.explanation: An upstream employment record is not complete downstream readiness.

options.text: All target accounts must already exist immediately
options.explanation: Creation timing and supported provisioning require their own results.

options.text: The employee automatically has every app role
options.explanation: Permissions depend on approved requirements and target enforcement.

options.text: Only the user's display name matters
options.explanation: Readiness includes state, relationships and actual application outcomes.

questions.prompt: An employee's Finance move takes effect next Monday. What should guide access changes?

options.text: The approved effective time and intended old/new access requirements
options.explanation: Do not treat a future business change as already effective.

options.text: Every source value should change immediately regardless of date
options.explanation: That ignores the approved timing constraint.

options.text: Keep all old access indefinitely
options.explanation: Old access needs an explicit retention or removal decision.

options.text: The new job title alone grants all Finance permissions
options.explanation: Business context is not a complete permission contract.

questions.prompt: A mover leaves one Sales group but retains a direct Sales app assignment. What should be checked?

options.text: Whether the remaining path is intended and approved
options.explanation: Removing one grant does not establish removal of all old access.

options.text: Assume the app is fully unassigned
options.explanation: The direct path can preserve assignment.

options.text: Delete the employee identity to remove one grant
options.explanation: That is broader than the supplied access problem.

options.text: Change the department back to Sales
options.explanation: The correct move should not be falsified to fit leftover access.

questions.prompt: An HR-led employee and an Okta-managed contractor both leave. Why can their procedures differ?

options.text: Their approved ownership and lifecycle relationships differ
options.explanation: A shared removal goal does not imply identical source-side actions.

options.text: Every contractor must first be added to employee HR
options.explanation: Do not invent a false association to imitate another population.

options.text: Only employees can have app sessions
options.explanation: Contractors can also have supported application sessions.

options.text: The same display label guarantees the same lifecycle behavior
options.explanation: Labels do not establish ownership and connector contracts.

questions.prompt: An employee is deactivated in Okta. What remains to verify?

options.text: Target account/access outcomes and relevant existing sessions under supported mechanisms
options.explanation: Provider lifecycle state does not prove every downstream termination.

options.text: Every app session necessarily ended instantly
options.explanation: That requires applicable revocation support and outcome evidence.

options.text: Every target account was physically deleted
options.explanation: Deactivation and deletion are distinct operations.

options.text: No downstream checks are needed once the source is updated
options.explanation: Each relevant target outcome still matters.

questions.prompt: Why distinguish disabling a target account from deleting it?

options.text: They have different resource, data-retention and recovery effects
options.explanation: Use the approved supported lifecycle operation rather than treating names as interchangeable.

options.text: Both always erase all stored business data
options.explanation: A disabled account can remain as a stored resource.

options.text: Deletion is always the safest default for every leaver
options.explanation: The correct action depends on approved policy and target behavior.

options.text: Deactivation always ends every session automatically
options.explanation: Session termination scope must be verified separately.

questions.prompt: A removed assignment blocks new SSO, but an old local app session still works. What boundary remains open?

options.text: The existing application's session termination or re-evaluation behavior
options.explanation: Future entry and current session continuity are distinct concerns.

options.text: The old assignment necessarily remains in Okta
options.explanation: An old local session can explain access after assignment removal.

options.text: The successful request proves a fresh SAML assertion was issued
options.explanation: Existing session access may involve no federation exchange.

options.text: Changing the HR manager automatically ends the session
options.explanation: That field change does not establish a revocation operation.

questions.prompt: A leaver update is queued for a target. What should the tracking record say?

options.text: The requested action is pending until its relevant completion is verified
options.explanation: Queued work must not be described as confirmed removal.

options.text: Access is already removed everywhere
options.explanation: The supplied record lacks that downstream evidence.

options.text: The target definitely rejected it
options.explanation: A pending state does not prove a failure either.

options.text: The employee has no identity in any system
options.explanation: A queued operation does not erase all records.

questions.prompt: A target does not support the desired automated deactivation. What is needed?

options.text: A documented approved manual or alternative removal process with an owner and verification
options.explanation: An unsupported connector capability does not remove the business obligation.

options.text: Assume Okta automatically invents the missing operation
options.explanation: Product support constrains what the integration can execute.

options.text: Close the leaver task because automation was attempted
options.explanation: Attempted work is not completed removal.

options.text: Give the user a different department to suppress the ticket
options.explanation: That falsifies facts instead of resolving access termination.

questions.prompt: HR departure is effective and Okta is deactivated, but no target result is supplied. What remains unknown?

options.text: Whether each relevant downstream account and session meets the removal requirement
options.explanation: Upstream completion does not establish unobserved target outcomes.

options.text: Whether the supplied departure is effective
options.explanation: That fact is explicitly stated.

options.text: Whether Okta was recorded as deactivated
options.explanation: That state is supplied directly.

options.text: Whether every record must be physically deleted
options.explanation: Physical deletion is not a universal consequence of departure.

questions.reasoning: Before choosing, explain which fact supports your conclusion and what the supplied evidence leaves unknown.
evidence: Target account and existing-session results: not supplied

questions.prompt: A former employee's fresh app sign-in is denied after verified removal. How should that test be recorded?

options.text: A successful rejection test under the removal requirement
options.explanation: Expected denial can demonstrate a correctly enforced boundary.

options.text: As proof the identity system needs reactivation
options.explanation: That would contradict the intended removal outcome.

options.text: As proof all old sessions are terminated
options.explanation: The fresh-entry test does not establish every existing session's state.

options.text: As an application outage for all users
options.explanation: One intended rejection does not establish a universal outage.

questions.prompt: After an employee departure, which handover most usefully establishes the access-removal status?

options.text: Named systems, required end states, actual results, owners and unresolved outcomes
options.explanation: Completion should be scoped to confirmed evidence, with open work visible.

options.text: Only the phrase access removed
options.explanation: That does not identify systems, sessions or verification.

options.text: Only a source screenshot
options.explanation: An upstream view does not establish target outcomes.

options.text: Only a proposed removal script
options.explanation: A proposal is not an execution and verification record.

questions.reasoning: Before choosing, explain which fact supports your conclusion and what the supplied evidence leaves unknown.
